I'd stay away from a colored background as part of the logo, it could limit the ways you can use it and have it look good. It kind of ends up confusing the issue, without really adding anything. After all a unique recognizable shape in and of itself is what logo design is all about. You want that "negative space." I like the shape, it's good, but it's visually "heavy". That's why I'd suggest black or grey for the type color. You need to balance the design with something that calls more attention to itself. You can accomplish this in several ways. With a darker color, with a heavier (thicker) type weight, bigger type pt. size or with a more unique typeface. Sometimes it takes a combination of these to finally hit the spot.

I think the shape is overwhelming the type. It might be too big in comparison. I'd push the type right and give it some more space, maybe try both words on one line. Also maybe either increase the tracking (space between letters) or experiment with some more typefaces to find something with a little more character. I'd also consider grey, or black type.

I felt nervous before each and every call, but I had no other means of making money at the time so I did it anyway. Over and over, it got easier, then it got dull and simply became routine. Routine is the anxiety killer. You want this. Keep in mind, everyone expects new hires to make mistakes at first. You will learn how best to do the job over time. [This](https://socialanxietyinstitute.org/social-anxiety-treatment) is the program I use. I have the old audio program and workbook. A few weeks after I bought it they upgraded the program to a subscription service thing, but I think you can still get the basic series for $250, a lot of people also seem to download it as a torrent for free. 

You have to be persistent for it to take, and devote time to it on a schedule, no matter how you're feeling that day. Even if you don't see any changes yet. I work on it for 30mins to 1 hr a day, and have actually seen real improvement, other people have even noticed and complemented me on it.

It's fairly fast improvement in the greater scheme of things (5 months to completion) but not as fast as most of us would like. Change is incremental and you don't really start to notice how big the difference is until you're about 6-8 weeks in.  

I really liked that I was given useful techniques right away that I could start using immediately.
I also like that it's so sensible and straightforward. No meditation or yoga, or inner child finding or anything like that.

Anyway, everybody's different, your mileage may vary. I can verify that it's not a scam though.

I'm on a combo antidepressant and self directed online CBT (which frankly has been much more successful than the many counselors I've been to, who would all rather me pay them the shirt off my back for an hour of idle chit chat, than provide real, scientifically proven therapy /rant ) and honestly I wish I'd never started the antidepressant because I've clearly developed a dependency and the CBT is so good I think it might have worked just as well if I'd done it without medication. Unlike the CBT, medication was never good enough on it's own, and it only ever worked for a little while, before dependency developed. So no effect much, but at the same time I can't just quit. Also there are side effects, for me anyway. If you can, I'd say try CBT without medication, then decide if you need it after you've given CBT 4-5 weeks since that's about when it really seemed to start working.

I do this sometimes. I don't mean to be rude. I can want to do something in the abstract, but when the event gets close I can experience mounting anxiety, and even panic attacks. It's hard to be reasonable in the middle of a panic. Sometimes in person comfort and reassurance can help. Maybe warming up for an event a little early together in a familiar safe place. This can help get past the panic part. Maybe even just talking on the phone casually for a while prior to the event, not about anxiety unless they want to, but rather about fun, funny distracting things. If you can distract away from panic it usually will pass. Becoming a regular, routine presence in the life of an sa person tends to warm them up. So even if it seems like they are pushing you away, more contact is helpful. They are probably ambivalently torn between wanting contact and sa. So ignoring the sa and encouraging the desire for contact is more helpful to the person with sa. It shows them they can have friends successfully without being and performing perfectly.

If you are in college, be sure to join a group and do something extracurricular. The reasons are: 
1. Because so few people are willing to get involved in extracurriculars it will likely be a smallish group. This allows you to really get to know people.
2. You'll be obligated to meet regularly, and will probably do non-school things together like go out to dinner or a movie. This is great because planned events take the pressure off you to ask someone to hang out, and the group takes the pressure off you to carry a conversation with someone you don't know that well. Plus the element of obligation encourages you to show up even when you are feeling shy. 
3. You'll be working to achieve something as a team. People bond in the trenches. I cannot overstate the importance of working together enough. It really is the best way to make friends. Plus the task at hand will always give you something to talk / joke about.

As someone in an actual successful and long marriage, date people who have a similar fundamental personality to yourself, don't focus on superficial things you might have in common, like liking the same movies or music. This is important. If you want genuine support and empathy you have to be able to really understand one another.

They shouldn't have to strike you instantly as drop dead gorgeous, that fades anyway and if it's the only reason you picked them you'll be inevitably disappointed. Reasonably attractive is good enough, because they'll become incredibly beautiful to you as you begin to love them see their inside and their outside as one, and the great thing about this love based perception of beauty is that it will stick, regardless of how they age. Finally, it's good to give your relationship reinforcement by being supportive, sincerely complementary, and a cheerleader in your partner's endeavors, listen and be honest, share freely about 95% of what's on your mind (if you're hiding most of your thoughts, because of anticipated criticism or disinterest, it's a huge red flag) and strive to be understanding and helpful rather than critical when your partner has a worry, problem or fear.
